THE OVERMAP

30 × 15 sectors · Each sector: 10 × 10 blocks · Each block: 24 × 24 tiles

STRATEGIC GENERATOR
LOCAL MAPS NOT ASSIGNED YET

Tutorial → rivers (4 edge connections) → cliffs (2) → environments → zones → settlements → roads → gates → validation. Towns and villages use 2 adjoining sectors. Easy: 2 towns (including start), 1 village, a 3-sector city. Medium: 1 town, 2 villages, 3–4 and 4-sector cities. Hard: 1 town, no villages, 3–4 and 5-sector cities. Different settlements require a one-sector gap, including diagonally. The easy fortress stays at least 4 sectors from the nearest starting-town sector, counting diagonal steps. All fortresses stay at least 4 sectors from each other, including diagonally. Crossing roads connect on both banks. Facilities occupy settlement sectors. Planned bridges round up to 1 per 5 river sectors and cannot touch diagonally. Settlements may occupy river sectors: they replace a planned bridge there or add an extra crossing.

Each seed chooses 1–5 environment families with equal chances for each count. Region sizes and positions vary independently of difficulty. Ground and foliage use the five painterly plant families. Preview a sector below, then paint density and passability in its local editor.

Preparing the initial seeded world…

Generation checks and limitations
Strategic connectivity treats river and cliff sectors as barriers crossed at gates. Local terrain, bank movement and eligible tactical sector templates still need integration. Each river and cliff receives its own independently sampled boundary endpoints before routing. Same-edge, adjacent-edge and opposite-edge paths are possible. Every river and cliff reaches at least two sectors inward from the nearest map edge somewhere along its route. Routes avoid the tutorial and other features. Each north/south edge position has weight 1; each east/west position has weight ½. Including edge lengths, the initial endpoint weights total 80% north/south and 20% east/west, before invalid layouts are retried. These are strategic plans, not playable campaigns.
